Executive Overview

The catalog has a strong baseline rating profile: average rating is 4.10, and 75.8% of products are rated 4.0 or above. Promotional intensity is high, with an average discount of 47.7% and median discount of 50.0%.

Best category signal

OfficeProducts leads rated categories with an average rating of 4.31 across 31 products.

Discount signal

Discount depth has a -0.155 correlation with rating, indicating limited satisfaction lift from deeper discounts.

Engagement signal

Electronics has the highest median engagement among ≥10-product categories at 10,689 ratings per product.

Headline implication: Satisfaction is more category- and product-experience-led than discount-led. Discounts appear more useful for visibility and review generation than for improving product ratings.

Pricing & Discount Strategy Analysis

This section quantifies whether pricing and promotional depth are associated with satisfaction or engagement. The strongest management takeaway is that discounting does not materially improve ratings in this dataset.

Correlation evidence: Discount percentage vs. rating has Pearson r=-0.155, while discount percentage vs. log review volume has r=-0.106. This supports using discounts selectively for demand generation, not as a substitute for product-quality improvements.

Review Sentiment Snapshot

Review fields are product-level text aggregates, so this is a directional keyword-based snapshot rather than a review-level sentiment model. Counts represent products whose review title/content mentions at least one theme keyword.

Theme interpretation

The most common theme is quality, appearing in 1424 products (97.2%). Use this as a prioritization cue for product detail pages, QA checks, and post-purchase issue triage.

Because each row can contain several comma-separated reviews, the theme count is best read as product coverage rather than number of individual reviews.

Strategic Recommendations

Each recommendation below is tied directly to observed data in the catalog.

Protect and expand high-satisfaction categories: OfficeProducts, Computers&Accessories, Electronics.

These categories lead the ≥10-product category set, with OfficeProducts averaging 4.31 stars across 31 products.

Treat deep discounting as an engagement lever, not a satisfaction lever.

Discount percentage has a -0.155 correlation with rating but a -0.106 correlation with log review volume; deeper discounts do not materially lift satisfaction in this catalog.

Audit the lowest-rated category: Home&Kitchen.

It averages 4.04 stars across 448 products, below the catalog average of 4.10.

Use price-tier playbooks; >₹5k products show the best satisfaction.

The >₹5k segment averages 4.17 stars with median engagement of 6,931 ratings.

Prioritize review-content fixes around the most common customer themes.

The most frequent review theme is quality, appearing in 1424 products (97.2% of the catalog).

Methodology & Data Quality

Data source: /app/benchmark/data.csv. The analysis parses rupee-denominated price fields, percentage discounts, customer rating counts, and hierarchical categories directly from the source file. Correlations use Pearson r after excluding missing values; review-volume correlations use log10 rating count to reduce skew. Missing or malformed ratings are excluded from rating calculations; 2 products have missing rating-count values.

All numbers in this report are calculated from /app/benchmark/data.csv; no external benchmarks or fabricated assumptions are used.
